Symptoms of childhood ependymoma depend on the stage of the tumor. The most common symptoms include: Abdominal pain, especially in the lower abdomen and lower back Pain in the upper abdomen and upper back

Symptoms of thymoma and thymic carcinoma may include: Abdominal pain, especially in the chest, abdomen, or abdomen Pain in the abdomen, abdomen or pelvis, or in the lower back Pain or tenderness in the back of the neck, neck, or upper back
Symptoms of polycythemia vera include: Abdominal pain or tenderness in the abdomen, abdomen, or pelvis Pain in the pelvis, groin, or back of the abdomen
Symptoms of Gastrointestinal Carcinoid Tumors may include: Abdominal pain Nausea and vomiting Diarrhea and vomiting
The outlook for metastatic squamous neck cancer with Occult Primary is generally good.
Symptoms of primary myelofibrosis depend on the type of the disease. The most common symptoms include: Abdominal pain, fever, and muscle aches.
Symptoms of childhood non-Hodgkin lymphoma may include: Abdominal pain or tenderness in the abdomen, abdomen, or pelvis Pain in the pelvis and pelvis

The most common symptoms of Merkel cell carcinoma are: Abdominal pain or tenderness in the abdomen, abdomen, or pelvis Pain in the pelvis or abdomen, especially in the lower abdomen, abdominal pain, and abdominal tenderness.
